summary: A survey of how many hosts accept Telnet connections from a user at a class C site. That requires working IP, TCP, gateway routing via ICMP and handling of class C addresses.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 844 reports tests of Telnet connections from a Class C network to hosts listed as accepting Telnet. It records which attempts worked, were refused, got no response, or were reported unreachable.

questions: how many hosts accepted telnet from the class c site
subtitle: A survey of Telnet connections from a Class C site to listed Internet hosts.

tldr.problem: A Telnet connection from a Class C site tests support for IP, TCP, ICMP gateway routing, and handling of Class C addresses together.
tldr.mechanism: The author tried connections from a terminal concentrator at BBN to hosts listed as accepting Telnet in RFC 843 and recorded the responses.
tldr.outcome: 127 of the 187 hosts tested accepted connections in the survey. The RFC presents the results as a snapshot from 18 February 1983.

today: RFC 844 records a Telnet connectivity survey conducted from a Class C site on 18 February 1983. Its results describe the hosts tested and the responses observed at that time.

sections.title: What the Survey Tested
sections.content:
The survey asked how many hosts could respond to Telnet connections from a Class C site. Success required more than Telnet: the test also depended on IP, TCP, ICMP gateway routing, and correct handling of Class C addresses.

The test computer was a terminal concentrator at 192.1.2.22 at BBN, connected to the Internet through a routing gateway that supported ICMP.
sections.plainLanguage: The survey tested whether hosts could accept a Telnet connection from a Class C network. That checked several Internet functions working together.

sections.title: Test Method
sections.content:
The author took hosts listed as accepting Telnet in RFC 843 and manually tried their dotted-form addresses on 18 February 1983 between 3 PM and 6:30 PM EST.

Only three passes were made through the host list. The report cautions that a host might have been missed because it was down during those attempts.
sections.plainLanguage: The tests were typed manually and repeated three times through the list. A host that was down at those times might not have been counted as reachable.

sections.title: Reported Results
sections.content:
Of 187 hosts tested, 127 accepted the connection, for a reported success rate of 67.9%. The table groups outcomes by network type: 77 of 121 on network 10 accepted, 20 of 34 on other Class A networks accepted, and 30 of 32 on non-Class A networks accepted.

The detailed table records each host's address and result as OK, refused, no response, or host unreachable.
sections.plainLanguage: Most tested hosts accepted the connection, but results varied by network group. The report lists each attempt's outcome as well as the totals.
